task.description: REQ-VALIDATOR gate over REQ-118, REQ-119, REQ-120, REQ-111 (criterion 3 amendment only). Apply your role's whole checklist: every criterion checkable by the named test or command and not by a person's taste; no criterion weaker than PLAN's acceptance lines and audit chapter 10 for the same thing (name each one compared); no production check as a criterion; no contradiction with another block, ARCH, a plan amendment or the ORCH answers; the owner's words quoted verbatim where relied on; the goal of decisions/0133 served and nothing outside it added; dependencies and order named; no secret, machine path or reference-product name. Re-derive at least three claims of the analyst's self_check yourself (for example the unchanged rest of the file by hash against HEAD~1 or the commit named in the handoff, a test file that a criterion says exists, a number). Verdict PASS or FAIL with findings by severity (blocking / non-blocking), each with the block, the criterion number, the problem and the exact change you want. Check also that the REQ-111 exception is as narrow as decisions/0136 О16 says and that the description of REQ-116 does not promise a wider one (say what must change if it does). The fact that this Windows PC has hardware virtualization off (Docker cannot start) is ORCH's measurement: no criterion may need the owner's PC as the host. Be economical. RULES OF THIS PC (decisions/0110, 0127, 0129): do NOT run npm run check, cd app && npm run ..., node --test, the tools test scripts or the e2e tests; the record of a test run is read from GitHub with gh run view (read-only). Allowed: cd tools && npm run -s traces and handoffs-check; read-only git and gh; your own scripts and fresh clones (git clone -c core.autocrlf=false, npm ci) only in your own folder under <scratch> (the real path is in the message that launched you). Node 22 first on PATH (<node22>). A server you start binds port 0 or a free high port and is stopped by its exact process id; never bind, probe or stop the ports 4780, 4781, 4782 and 4790. One browser at a time on this PC. No git commit, push, pull, checkout, stash, reset or tag. LF line endings. Never write the name of the reference product, nor a path of this computer, into a Sai file or a handoff (write <scratch> or <outside the project>). Fill only the result of your handoff; the top-level status stays PENDING and completed_at null: ORCH closes. English.

findings.requirement: REQ-120 (description «A previous-schema mode compares only the tables of A»; criteria 1 and 3)
findings.problem: Criterion 3 needs the previous-schema comparison to end with exit 0 after an expand-only migration and to be red for a migration that drops a seeded column. As written the mode cannot do both: (1) schema_migrations is a table of A, and B holds one row more (the newest migration), so «per table the row count» and «schema_migrations names and sha256 equal» give 1 on every rehearsal; (2) the content sha256 is taken only for the closed list of tables, so a dropped column of any other table is not seen, while a column added to a closed-list table changes every row's content hash and gives a false red; (3) criterion 1 has no case of the previous-schema mode at all.
findings.needed: Fix in the block what the previous-schema mode compares: how schema_migrations is read (the rows of A are a prefix of B's), whether it compares A's columns only (a dropped or retyped column of any table of A is a difference, an added column is not), and what it does with row counts; and add unit cases of that mode to app/test/unit/db-verify.test.js (an additive migration -> 0; a dropped column, a dropped table, a deleted row -> 1).

findings.problem: The amended criterion says the consent keys «are named once, in one frozen constant of app/scripts/word-lists.js that check-public and app/test/unit/forbidden-words.test.js both read». No such constant exists: `grep -n -i consent app/scripts/word-lists.js app/scripts/check-public.js app/test/unit/forbidden-words.test.js` prints nothing. The status stays done with the claim «while the constant is empty the lint of the real files is unchanged, so the released code still meets the criterion» — it does not: a RELEASE-VALIDATOR reading the criterion today finds no constant and no reader of it.
findings.needed: Either the amendment says that the constant, its reading by check-public and by the test are created by the work of REQ-116 (and that until then the criterion is the text before the amendment), so the done status stays true; or the status line stops claiming the criterion is met by the released code.
